thought.text: LDAP works with the compose defaults. The app's config is stale (planetexpress:10389). Let me align the local config to the running LDAP.

reasoning_content:
LDAP works with openldap:389, admin/admin, dc=example,dc=org, and 10 entries. Now align the app config. The local config currently overrides with planetexpress defaults (commented out — actually the whole 'ldap' block is commented out in local config, so Page config falls back to web.config.php's ldap block which is planetexpress). So effective LDAP = planetexpress:10389. Need to change config/web.config.local.php to uncomment a correct ldap block.

Let me set the local config ldap to match: host 'openldap', port 389, dn 'cn=admin,dc=example,dc=org', password 'admin', baseDn 'dc=example,dc=org', filter '(&(objectClass=inetOrgPerson)(description=Human))'. But the compose test users don't have `description=Human`! The filter in config requires description=Human. test_users.ldif has no description. Hmm. That's why the planetexpress config had description=Human (planetexpress demo users have description). The provided test_users.ldif doesn't include description, so filter must not require it.

Wait — bind dn in local config example is 'cn=admin,dc=planetexpress,dc=com'. The comment block wasn't necessarily "correct". Let me design the local override to work with test_users.ldif.

Filter used in search: default filter from config. In BenutzerNeu ldapSearch, it calls search(null, '(mail=*)') → filter becomes '(&(mail=*)(<defaultFilter>))'. If default filter requires description=Human, no results. So set filter to something that matches, e.g. '(&(objectClass=inetOrgPerson))' or just '(objectClass=*)'. Actually the search combines: since passed filter '(mail=*)' doesn't contain defaultFilter, result = '(&(mail=*)(defaultFilter))'. So set filter = '(objectClass=inetOrgPerson)'. Then combined = '(&(mail=*)(objectClass=inetOrgPerson))' matches 10 users. 

The test types search_string 'Mustermann' but the app ignores it and searches (mail=*). Fine.

Let me update config/web.config.local.php with an active ldap block:
```php
'ldap' => [
    'host' => 'openldap',
    'port' => 389,
    'serverType' => Dsl\App\Tools\LdapUtility::SERVERTYPE_OPENLDAP,
    'dn' => 'cn=admin,dc=example,dc=org',
    'password' => 'admin',
    'baseDn' => 'dc=example,dc=org',
    'filter' => '(objectClass=inetOrgPerson)',
],
```

Note config/web.config.php has 'ldap.host' => 'ldap'. In the ddev network, is there a hostname 'ldap'? The compose service is 'openldap'. ddev may add alias 'ldap'? getent earlier: "getent hosts ldap openldap" returned only openldap -> 172.19.0.2. So host must be 'openldap'.

Let me update and clear cache, then re-run.

action.command:
cd /workspace; cat > config/web.config.local.php <<'PHP'
<?php

/** @var  $configLocal Überschreibt $config-Einträge aus web.config.php */
$configLocal = array (
    'ldap' => [
        'host' => 'openldap',
        'port' => 389,
        'serverType' => Dsl\App\Tools\LdapUtility::SERVERTYPE_OPENLDAP,
        'dn' => 'cn=admin,dc=example,dc=org',
        'password' => 'admin',
        'baseDn' => 'dc=example,dc=org',
        'filter' => '(objectClass=inetOrgPerson)',
    ]
);
PHP
cat config/web.config.local.php
rm -rf cache/compile/* cache/smarty/* 2>/dev/null; echo "cache cleared"
